habit_scope: Low-slope or flat: roof joists serve as ceiling joists. CMHC Ch11 Low-Slope Roofs is a real construction type (slope at least 1:50). AF&PA Flat Roofs: should be avoided if possible (vent, insulation, weatherproofing). HUD lists timber framing separately — not this method. Not the volume truss habit. Not Fontana snow-pack related.
how_it_is_done: Walls complete. AF&PA: where flat roofs are used, rafters or roof joists serve as ceiling joists for the space below (Fig 59). Nail to exterior wall plates and to each other where they join over interior partitions.

CMHC: size from roof AND ceiling loads (Tables 29-30 Canadian). Depth may need to grow for insulation + ventilation even if structure is OK. Slope at least 1:50 for drainage — ledger strip at the bearing wall or tapered strip on the joists.
Lookout rafters for the overhang (CMHC Fig 91; AF&PA Fig 59 lookouts to a double trimmer). If lookouts project more than one-and-one-half joist spaces, double the inner joists as a header.

Ventilate. AF&PA: blocking/bridging/insulation arranged so air is not blocked; eave soffit net open area 1/250 of the ceiling; vapor retarder 1 perm or less under the ceiling finish. CMHC: 63 mm (2-1/2 in) ventilated space above batt insulation; or rigid insulation on top of the sheathing (then the space above the ceiling is not ventilated). Confirm AHJ. Attic vent ratios live partly in P13 — do not invent IRC R806.
AF&PA: avoid if possible. This is the sourced SFR alt when the drawings are flat/low-slope, not a cheaper skip of a pitched truss.
Sheathing is m-P09-roof-sheathing. Built-up / membrane coverings named in CMHC/FM are P11 finish, not this framing method.
tools_equipment: Not a tool list in sources.
inspection_hold_points: Roof joists nailed to plates and over interior partitions (AF&PA).
Drainage slope at least 1:50 (CMHC) — Canadian / confirm AHJ.
Vent path not blocked (AF&PA 1/250 eaves; CMHC 2-1/2 in over batts).
Lookouts to a doubled trimmer when they run past 1.5 spaces (CMHC; AF&PA Fig 59).
material_classes: tapered strip or ledger for drainage slope
when_this_beats_habit: When the drawings are a deck, terrace, or low-slope (CMHC). Not because it is cheaper than trusses.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: AF&PA: avoid if possible — hard to vent, insulate, and weatherproof. Using it to skip a pitched truss on a 2-story habit house. Copying Utah ice onto Fontana. Built-up tar as this framing method.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They frame decks. What they skip is the 1:50 drain slope and the vent gap above the insulation.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Low-slope vs pitched is permit-gate. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. CMHC tables are Canadian. Do not invent IRC R803.
risk_if_swapped_late: Flat vs pitched after permit changes drainage, insulation depth, and covering class. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: A low-slope or flat roof uses joists that are also the ceiling. Drain it at least 1 in 50. Leave a vent gap over the insulation. The AF&PA book says avoid a flat roof if you can — this is the alt when the drawings are actually flat, not a cheaper skip of trusses.
spanish_summary: Techo plano o de poca pendiente: las viguetas son tambien el cielo. Drenaje minimo 1 en 50. Deje hueco de ventilacion sobre el aislante. AF&PA dice evitarlo si puede — es la alternativa cuando el plano es plano, no un ahorro de cerchas.

AF&PA ventilation of flat roofs 1/250 at eaves (txt 847-851).
